To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SR Ca release channel is a voltage-gated Ca channel that is regulated by Ca inactivation and that the Ca-dependent acceleration of release inactivation is due to a decrease in the rate of Ca binding to the inactivation gate of the channel.
the fractional rate and time course of SR Ca release are regulated by [Ca] in the immediate environment of the SR Ca channels.

the amount of Ca released by an action potential is determined by the amount of Ca stored in the SR, that Ca inactivation of release is increased by increasing myoplasmic [Ca], and that Ca inactivation and the action potential are regulated by Ca within 22 nm from the mouth of the Ca release channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the Ca released from the sarcoplasmic (SR) Ca stores of muscle is regulated by Ca.
the mechanisms of excitation–contraction coupling, and the role of the sarcoplasmic Ca release channels in these mechanisms.
the mechanisms of excitation–contraction coupling and the effects of Ca feedback on these mechanisms in cut muscle fibers of the frog.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of [CaSR] on the kinetics of Ca release are complex and depend on the history of the muscle fiber.

, after an action potential, Ca release is slowed by a combination of Ca inactivation, acceleration of Q cm, and reduction of the action potential, all three of which are regulated by the amount of Ca in the myoplasm.
Ca is a positive regulator of the voltage sensor and a negative regulator of the Ca release channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in cut fibers equi-librated with 20 mM external EGTA, the value of [SR Ca]R that is required for maximal SR Ca release is reduced by a factor of 8, from 1,600 μM in normal physiological condition to 200 μM in fibers equilibrated at 20 mM EG- TA.
the SR Ca release channel is a complex structure with multiple sites of Ca regulation, some of which are close to the mouth of the release channel and some of which are not.
the effects of Ca on the SR Ca channel are complex and that the Ca sensitivity of the channel is regulated by [Ca] in the immediate vicinity of the channel mouth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of [Ca] on SR Ca release are more complex than previously appreciated.

the SR Ca release process has a negative feedback mechanism that is sensitive to the value of [free]Ca in the immediate vicinity of the release channel, and this mechanism can be activated even when [free]Ca is only a small fraction (10–15%) of the value that is normally present in a muscle fiber.
, when CaSR Ca content is reduced from 1.2 to 0.14 mM, SR Ca release is increased by a factor of 3, and the release kinetics is prolonged by a factor of ∼6.
